centring: Treatment indicators centred at the empirical share of each treatment level among available decision points (constant over time), with p_tilde = p (unit weights). The design randomisation probabilities are not verified from the paper text in this session.
comparison_rule: consistent if log(1 + published_percent/100) lies inside our 95% cluster-bootstrap CI for the corresponding term; the primary comparison is any_suggestion.
estimand: Marginal causal excursion effect (Boruvka et al. 2018) of A_t = suggestion delivered at an available decision point on Y_t = log(jbsteps30.zero + 0.5), averaged over study days and suggestion types; secondary: walking and anti-sedentary suggestions vs none; time-moderated effect (study day).
falsification_criterion: Fails if the published estimate (log scale) lies outside our 95% participant-cluster bootstrap CI.
hypothesis: A centred least-squares estimate of the causal excursion effect of delivering an activity suggestion (vs none) on log 30-minute step count, computed from the public HeartSteps V1 data, is consistent with the effect published by Klasnja et al. (2019).
identification_assumptions: Treatment was randomised at each available decision point (micro-randomised trial design), so A_t is independent of potential outcomes given availability.
Consistency and no interference between participants.
The estimand is a causal excursion effect conditional on availability, marginal over the realised treatment history; it is not a total effect of the HeartSteps programme.
Zero-imputation of missing tracker minutes (jbsteps30.zero) follows the dataset's provided columns; complete-case is a sensitivity analysis.

published.source: Klasnja et al. 2019, Ann Behav Med 53(6):573-582, abstract (PubMed PMID 30192907), retrieved 2026-11-04
published.verified_text: Averaging over study days and types of activity suggestions, delivering a suggestion versus no suggestion increased the 30-min step count by 14% (p = .06), 35 additional steps over the 253-step average.
Averaging over study days, delivering a walking suggestion versus no suggestion increased the average step count by 24% (59 steps; p = .02).

sensitivity: complete-case outcome log(jbsteps30 + 0.5) (rows with missing Jawbone minutes dropped)
title: Can our causal-estimation pipeline recover the published HeartSteps V1 suggestion effect?
validity_notes: The public dataset contains 37 participants; the paper reports a 6-week MRT with 44 adults. The analysed samples may differ.
The paper's exact control covariates and outcome transform are not verified from its full text in this session (only the abstract was accessible).
This is the only real causal estimate in the repository. It is not mixed with, and does not validate, any simulation result.
